$comment: Golden contract fixture for GET /api/health (mt#2629). Single shared location consumed by BOTH sides of the tray/cockpit supervision split: src/cockpit/health-contract.test.ts (bun) asserts the LIVE server response's field set + types match `fields` below; cockpit-tray/src-tauri/src/supervisor.rs's `health_contract` test module (cargo) asserts these fields — plus the literal TS source of health.ts — still name the fields the Rust supervisor parses (`rustConsumedFields`). See contract/README.md for the full contract note, including the port/process-detection semantics documented alongside this fixture.
$transcriptWatcherFieldNote: mt#3857: unlike the other nested objects here, this one IS type-asserted — `transcriptWatcherFields` above is enforced by health-contract.test.ts, because this sub-object caused a real payload defect and a loose `object` pin is what let it through. `activeSessions` carries only the LIVE subset (entries whose `lastEventAt` is within LIVE_SESSION_WINDOW_MS, 2 min, per transcript-watcher-tracker.ts), NOT the full registry; `activeSessionCount` carries the registry total. Before mt#3857 `activeSessions` WAS the full registry: it reached 1,380 entries / 209 KB, which is 99.5% of a response the tray supervisor polls every 5s and three webview query keys poll every 15s. Two invariants a consumer — or a future edit — must preserve: (1) the array is bounded by the recency window, never by the registry size, so this response does not grow with transcript history; (2) `activeSessionCount` is the ONLY place the total is reported, so a consumer wanting 'how many conversations does the watcher know about' reads the scalar and must not infer it from the array length. The boot scan seeds via recordSessionSeeded() with a null lastEventAt precisely so a restart does not make the whole history look live and re-inflate this array.
$dbFieldNote: mt#3563: `db` reports LIVE reachability as of the last probe, not a boot-time constant. "ok" = a query completed through the SHARED pool inside the probe deadline; "degraded" = one did not (timed out, errored, or a previously issued probe has still not returned — the never-settling-query wedge of mt#3092/mt#2773); "unreachable" = no init has ever succeeded. Before mt#3563 this was set once at init and only left "ok" on a circuit-breaker rejection, so a daemon whose every DB route hung reported "ok" indefinitely (incidents 2026-08-01 and 2026-08-03) and the tray's DB-degraded watchdog never fired. Two properties consumers depend on and must not 'optimize' away: (1) the HTTP status stays 200 regardless of `db` — ADR-014 makes the status code the tray's liveness/adoption signal, so DB truth belongs in the body, exactly as `schema` does; (2) the probe runs OUT-OF-BAND and the handler never awaits it, so this route cannot be made slow by the database it reports on. Consequence: `db` lags reality by at most one poll, which is why `dbCheck.checkedAt` exists — an `ok` you cannot date is the same false confidence this field was fixed to remove.
$dbCheckFieldNote: mt#3563: `dbCheck` is always an OBJECT (never null), but BOTH of its members are nullable and a consumer must handle each. `checkedAt` (ISO string | null) is null until the first probe FINISHES, and thereafter names when reachability was last actually determined — it is deliberately NOT restamped on a poll that merely observes an earlier probe still outstanding, so during a wedge it goes stale on purpose; stale `checkedAt` + `db: "degraded"` reads as 'stuck since then', which is the intended signal, not a gap. `latencyMs` (number | null) is the round-trip of the last SUCCESSFUL probe and stays null until one succeeds — it is NOT reset when a later probe fails, so a non-null `latencyMs` alongside `db: "degraded"` describes the last good measurement, not the current state. Read `db` for current state and `dbCheck` for its provenance; do not infer health from `latencyMs` alone.
$dbRecycleFieldNote: mt#3638: `dbRecycle` reports the wedge-triggered pool recycle (the recovery half of mt#3563's detection). Always an object; `lastRecycleAt` (ISO string | null) is null until the first recycle this process, `recycleCount` (number) counts recycles since process start. A non-zero count means the daemon detected sustained DB degradation and rebuilt its connection pool in place instead of waiting for a restart; a count that keeps rising while `db` stays degraded means recycling is not helping — the DB itself (or the network path) is down, which is the case the recycle deliberately does not try to fix.
$schemaFieldNote: mt#3297: `schema.current` is TRI-STATE — true (every shipped migration applied), false (the DB is behind this build, `pending` names which), or null (readiness could not be determined; `unknownReason` says why). A consumer that treats null as true reintroduces the bug this field exists to surface: the daemon boots fine and answers 200 while every schema-dependent write fails, so the status code cannot carry this and the body has to. Handle all three explicitly — true: proceed; false: the DB needs `minsky persistence migrate --execute`, and schema-dependent sweeps are paused; null: state unknown, treat as 'cannot vouch for it' rather than as either healthy or broken.
$principalChannelFieldNote: mt#3608 introduced this field; mt#3683 removed its retry CEILING. `state` is one of disabled/starting/running/unconfigured/retrying/failed. `unconfigured`/`disabled` are healthy-quiet states; `retrying` and `failed` are faults, but different ones. `retrying` means a credential read failed and is classified TRANSIENT — per ADR-035 rule 1 it no longer gives up on its own: past the original ~2-minute/6-attempt window it keeps retrying on a widening, capped backoff instead of settling into `failed`, for as long as the fault persists. `lastAttemptAt`/`nextAttemptAt` (ISO strings, present ONLY on `retrying`, per ADR-035 rule 4) are what make 'still actively working the problem' legible without parsing `reason` prose or inferring it from a possibly-stale `attempts` count — a `nextAttemptAt` in the near future is the discriminator between 'retrying' and 'stuck'. `failed` is now a DIFFERENT fault class entirely: an exception raised AFTER credentials resolved (poller/actuator construction), not reachable from a credential-read failure any more, since that path no longer exhausts. mt#3689 REMOVED `attempts` from the `failed` variant: it was always the literal 1 there and counted nothing (the failure happens once, after credentials already resolved), so one field was carrying two meanings across two fault classes. `state` already separates them. `attempts` is now present ONLY on `retrying`, where it is a real count of credential reads. Note that this sub-object's shape is documented HERE and is NOT type-asserted by either contract test — those pin the TOP-LEVEL field set (`principalChannel: object`) plus `rustConsumedFields`, so a change inside this object must be reflected in this block by hand.

unconfigured.reason: Telegram principal channel is not configured: neither TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID are set in the environment, nor are the Pulumi stack values set.

retrying.reason: Telegram principal channel credentials could not be READ (this is not the same as them being unset): chat-id read failed: exit null. The channel will retry.
